evidence: chapter-02/chapter-02.md:164 reads verbatim 'Lowering precision (FP8, or BF16 in place of FP16) ... rather it reduces the precision, lowers the bytes transferred/stored, and can raise the effective accelerator throughput (8-bit tensor cores run at higher peak rate).' BF16 and FP16 are both 16-bit/2 B and share H100's 989 TFLOPS dense tensor-core peak, so 'lowers the bytes' and 'raises throughput' cannot apply to the BF16 example.
fix_instruction: In chapter-02/chapter-02.md:164 restrict the parenthetical to FP8 and give BF16 the correct trade-off, e.g.: 'Lowering byte-width precision (e.g. FP8) ... lowers the bytes transferred/stored and can raise effective throughput (8-bit tensor cores run at higher peak rate); changing format at the same width (BF16 in place of FP16) changes neither bytes nor peak throughput, it trades mantissa bits (10 -> 8) for exponent range.'

evidence: chapter-05/chapter-05.md §2 reads 'If the workload is input-heavy ..., the system is first-order memory‑capacity‑bound (the KV cache's HBM footprint limits how many concurrent requests fit — KV HBM capacity limits concurrency, not bandwidth — at the Ch 17 concurrency screen) and prefill‑dominated in FLOPs — a first-order tendency to verify per workload, not a consequence of input-heaviness alone.' The scope and the 'verify per workload' hedge are both present in the same sentence, so the conditional reading the finding asks for is already available.

chapter-06/chapter-06.md:131 first calls prefix caching 'a partial mitigation (~13% of prefill FLOPs), not the fix', names the resolution as 'capacity/scheduling — additional hosts, chunked prefill, admission control/backpressure, or P/D disaggregation', then closes 'the mechanism check confirms it — prefix-cache hit ratio ~13% and the predicted ~13% prefill reduction explain the 2.4 s -> <2 s move'. Recomputed from the same paragraph's own figures: 40 × 1.29 = 51.6 PFLOP/s demand vs ~2.77 PFLOP/s capacity = 18.6× oversubscribed; 13% off that demand is 44.9 PFLOP/s, still 16.2× — so the named resolution is never confirmed and the 13% cannot by itself carry the SLO recovery.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the mechanism-check sentence at chapter-06/chapter-06.md:131 to confirm the capacity/scheduling change actually made (e.g. host count added and the resulting oversubscription ratio, or the chunked-prefill/admission-control effect on queueing), and demote prefix caching to a contributing factor ('with the ~13% prefill reduction from prefix caching'), consistent with the same paragraph's 'not the fix'.
